title: ObjectSchema
description: A schema node of type 'object' that constrains JSON object instances by declaring a set of named, typed properties, which of those properties must be present, and rules for undeclared or dynamically named keys. In code it corresponds to a structured domain record (entity class, ORM model, DTO, record or interface with fields), not to an individual field or to a primitive type alias. Use SchemaProperty instead when the symbol is a single field, column or attribute inside a structure rather than the structure that owns the fields. Use JSONSchema instead when the element is the root schema document or file, identified by $schema and $id and holding definitions, rather than one object shape described within it. Use SchemaDefinition instead when the named reusable type is a primitive alias or enumeration (e.g. a TypeScript enum, a branded string type, a Python Enum) with no named fields of its own. Use SchemaComposition instead when the type is defined only by combining other schemas (union, intersection, discriminated oneOf, negation) rather than by declaring its own properties; plain class inheritance stays an objectschema with an extends relationship.

type.description: The JSON Schema type keyword, which is always the string 'object' for this element; set it on every instance.

properties.description: Named property definitions for the object schema (primary mechanism for defining object structure)

patternProperties.description: Pattern-matched property definitions applied to properties whose names match the given regex

propertyNames.description: Schema applied to all property names of the object instance for name validation

required.description: Array of property names (strings) that must be present in a valid instance; populate it from fields that are non-optional in code, such as TypeScript fields without '?', Pydantic fields without defaults, or NOT NULL columns.

additionalProperties.description: Either a boolean or a subschema (inline or $ref) governing keys not listed in properties or patternProperties; set false for closed models (e.g. Pydantic extra='forbid', TypeScript exact types) and a value schema for map-like types such as Record<string, T>. This schema stores the value as a single string.

minProperties.description: Non-negative integer giving the minimum number of keys a valid instance must contain; set it only when code or a validator explicitly enforces a lower bound on key count.

maxProperties.description: Non-negative integer giving the maximum number of keys a valid instance may contain; set it only when code or a validator explicitly enforces an upper bound on key count.

x-dr-standard: JSON Schema Draft 7 Validation (draft-handrews-json-schema-validation-01) §6.5 Validation Keywords for Objects
x-dr-evidence: A class annotated @Entity/@Table, a Django models.Model subclass, or a SQLAlchemy declarative class whose attributes declare domain fields
A TypeScript interface or type literal, Pydantic BaseModel, Python @dataclass, Java record, or Go struct with named typed fields used as a DTO or request/response payload
A JSON Schema or OpenAPI components.schemas entry with "type": "object" and a "properties" map, or a z.object()/Joi.object()/yup.object() validator declaration
